course.title: World Humanities, Culture & Ethical Inquiry
course.scope: comparative world humanities; no single-civilization canon is treated as universal authority

modules.title: Humanities as Inquiry
modules.essential: How literature, philosophy, history, art and cultural study ask different questions about human experience.

lessons.title: What Counts as a Humanities Question?
lessons.focus: Distinguish interpretive, historical, ethical and aesthetic questions from purely factual ones.

lessons.title: Texts, Artifacts and Contexts
lessons.focus: Treat written, visual, oral and material works as evidence situated in time and culture.

lessons.title: Interpretation and Evidence
lessons.focus: Support interpretation with specific features of a work and relevant context.

modules.title: Origins, Memory & Story
modules.essential: How communities use stories, myths, epics and memory to explain identity and order.

lessons.title: Myth, Epic and Foundational Narrative
lessons.focus: Compare how origin stories encode values, conflict and social imagination.

lessons.title: Oral Tradition and Cultural Memory
lessons.focus: Study how memory changes when knowledge moves through performance and retelling.

lessons.title: Archive, Silence and Survival
lessons.focus: Ask whose voices are preserved, omitted or mediated by surviving evidence.

modules.title: World Literature & Close Reading
modules.essential: How close reading reveals structure, voice, image, form and ambiguity.

lessons.title: Voice, Perspective and Reliability
lessons.focus: Analyze who speaks, from where, and with what limits.

lessons.title: Image, Symbol and Motif
lessons.focus: Interpret recurring language and imagery without reducing a work to one fixed meaning.

lessons.title: Form, Genre and Expectation
lessons.focus: Examine how genre shapes what readers anticipate and how meaning is produced.

modules.title: Philosophy & the Human Condition
modules.essential: How philosophical traditions frame knowledge, reality, selfhood and the good life.

lessons.title: Knowledge, Doubt and Justification
lessons.focus: Compare ways traditions distinguish belief, knowledge and wisdom.

lessons.title: Self, Mind and Identity
lessons.focus: Explore competing accounts of personhood and continuity.

lessons.title: Meaning, Mortality and the Good Life
lessons.focus: Compare ethical and existential approaches to living well.

modules.title: Ethics & Moral Reasoning
modules.essential: How people reason about duties, consequences, character, care and justice.

lessons.title: Consequences, Duties and Rules
lessons.focus: Compare outcome-based and duty-based moral reasoning.

lessons.title: Virtue, Character and Human Flourishing
lessons.focus: Examine ethical traditions centered on habits, character and flourishing.

lessons.title: Care, Relationship and Responsibility
lessons.focus: Analyze moral reasoning grounded in dependency, care and social relationship.

modules.title: Power, Society & Political Thought
modules.essential: How humanities traditions examine authority, freedom, justice and social order.

lessons.title: Authority and Legitimacy
lessons.focus: Compare accounts of why political or social authority should be obeyed or resisted.

lessons.title: Freedom, Equality and Justice
lessons.focus: Examine tensions among liberty, equality, rights and social obligation.

lessons.title: Empire, Resistance and Liberation
lessons.focus: Study how texts and thinkers interpret domination, resistance and decolonization.

modules.title: Religion, Ritual & Worldview
modules.essential: How religious and philosophical worldviews shape meaning, practice and community.

lessons.title: Ritual, Practice and Community
lessons.focus: Study religion through lived practice as well as doctrine.

lessons.title: Sacred Texts and Interpretation
lessons.focus: Compare interpretive traditions without treating one reading as the only possible one.

lessons.title: Pluralism, Secularism and Coexistence
lessons.focus: Examine how societies negotiate multiple religious and nonreligious worldviews.

modules.title: Art, Aesthetics & Visual Culture
modules.essential: How images, objects, architecture and performance communicate values and experience.

lessons.title: Seeing, Description and Formal Analysis
lessons.focus: Describe visual evidence before interpreting it.

lessons.title: Beauty, Taste and Aesthetic Judgment
lessons.focus: Compare philosophical accounts of aesthetic value and taste.

lessons.title: Art, Patronage and Public Meaning
lessons.focus: Connect artworks to institutions, markets, audiences and political contexts.

modules.title: History, Place & Mobility
modules.essential: How travel, migration, geography and exchange shape cultural interpretation.

lessons.title: Travel Writing and the Gaze
lessons.focus: Examine how travelers describe unfamiliar peoples and places.

lessons.title: Migration, Diaspora and Belonging
lessons.focus: Study identity and memory across displacement and multiple homes.

lessons.title: Exchange, Translation and Cultural Contact
lessons.focus: Analyze adaptation, borrowing, hybridity and unequal exchange.

modules.title: Language, Translation & Interpretation
modules.essential: How language mediates access to other times, cultures and ideas.

lessons.title: Translation as Interpretation
lessons.focus: Recognize that translation involves choices, losses and gains.

lessons.title: Untranslatable Terms and Cultural Concepts
lessons.focus: Avoid assuming that similar words carry identical meanings across cultures.

lessons.title: Comparative Reading Across Versions
lessons.focus: Use multiple translations or editions to expose interpretive choices.

modules.title: Memory, Museums & Public Humanities
modules.essential: How societies curate the past through monuments, archives, museums and public narratives.

lessons.title: Museums, Archives and Selection
lessons.focus: Analyze how collections create narratives through inclusion and omission.

lessons.title: Monuments, Commemoration and Contest
lessons.focus: Examine why public memory becomes a site of disagreement.

lessons.title: Digital Humanities and Public Access
lessons.focus: Consider how digitization changes preservation, discovery and interpretation.

modules.title: Comparative Humanities Capstone
modules.essential: How to synthesize texts, contexts and ethical questions into a defensible comparative interpretation.

lessons.title: Comparative Question and Source Dossier
lessons.focus: Build a focused question using works from more than one culture, period or medium.

lessons.title: Interpretive Essay or Public Humanities Project
lessons.focus: Create an evidence-based comparative interpretation for an identified audience.

lessons.title: Capstone Defense and Reflective Synthesis
lessons.focus: Defend interpretive choices, acknowledge limits and reflect on how context changed understanding.

assessment.capstone: comparative source dossier + interpretive essay/public humanities project + defense
